mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% signals tightening labor market conditions, increasing wage pressures and corporate labor costs, which leads to higher inflation expectations and subsequent equity market repricing, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE is 9.1 at t-1mo, indicating a high starting point for potential decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative or flat 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE falls below 5.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a tightening monetary policy regime, which reduces liquidity and raises discount rates, leading to lower equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:FEDFUNDS is 0.07 at t-1mo, well below 3.0, indicating potential for future rise
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both residential investment (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals strong underlying demand momentum, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST is 629.0 at t-2mo, RSAFS is 390422.0 at t-1mo, both indicating elevated demand
failure_condition: S&P 500 fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS rise, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity and broad supply-side contraction, which reduces corporate output and signals economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO is 93.07 at t-2mo, close to 90.0 threshold
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls below 90.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) combined with a rising GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates strong aggregate demand expansion, which drives corporate revenue growth and earnings upgrades, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:GDPC1 is 13270.1 at t-4mo, RSAFS is 390422.0 at t-1mo, both indicating robust demand
failure_condition: S&P 500 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both RSAFS and GDPC1 rise, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k per month signals strong labor market demand, which boosts consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:PAYEMS is 131190.0 at t-1mo, indicating strong labor market activity
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS exceeds 200.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting the Fed to maintain or raise rates, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:CPIAUCSL is 224.304 at t-2mo, indicating moderate inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, reducing corporate output and employment, which lowers earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO is 93.07 at t-2mo, UNRATE is 9.1 at t-1mo, both indicating stress
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
